title: Sindhu Cruises Past Sophia Noble in World Championships Opener
indian_angle: India's premier shuttler P.V. Sindhu began her quest for a historic sixth World Championships medal with a comfortable first-round victory.
summary: P.V. Sindhu won her first match at the BWF World Championships, defeating Sophia Noble 21-7, 21-11, as she aims for a record sixth medal in front of home fans.

title: Giantkiller Ayush Shetty Stuns World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi at Worlds
indian_angle: Indian debutant Ayush Shetty achieved a historic upset by defeating the reigning world champion and top seed in front of a home crowd.
summary: World No. 22 Ayush Shetty used powerful smashes and dogged defence to become the first to oust a reigning world champion and top seed in the first round of the World Championships, marking a historic debut.

title: Simran Singhi's Long Journey to World Championships Debut
indian_angle: Indian shuttler Simran Singhi shares her arduous path to the World Championships, aiming to prove her rightful place on the global stage.
summary: Simran Singhi opens up about her long journey to the 2026 Badminton World Championships, her partnership with Kavipriya Selvam, and her dream of proving she belongs.

title: Antonsen Blames Season, Not Delhi, for World Championships Pullouts
indian_angle: World No. 4 Anders Antonsen discusses the air pollution concerns in Delhi, which is hosting the World Championships, and suggests a shift in the tournament's timing.
summary: World No. 4 Antonsen has skipped the last three India Open tournaments citing air pollution in Delhi in January and hopes that the tournament is shifted to August, stating the problem is the season, not the city.

title: India's World Championships Return Marked by Ayush Shetty's Upset
indian_angle: The BWF World Championships in New Delhi began on a high note for India, highlighted by Ayush Shetty's sensational upset victory and the roaring home crowd.
summary: The BWF World Championships in New Delhi kicked off on an auspicious note for the home shuttlers with Ayush Shetty taking the badminton world by storm, marking India's return to hosting the event after 17 years.

title: Treesa Jolly, Gayatri Gopichand's Road Back to Worlds After Injury
indian_angle: India’s top women’s doubles pair, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, are rebuilding their form after an ankle injury sidelined Treesa, as they prepare for the World Championships.
summary: India’s top women’s doubles pair is rebuilding after an ankle injury had sidelined Treesa for a few months, as they launch their World Championships quest.
